sections.title: Seeking Hashem Through the Darkness of Creation
sections.summary: The hidden divine light makes room for human effort, free choice, and the sanctification of embodied life.

topics.h: Opening Text
topics.en: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. And the earth was unformed and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep..”

topics.h: Why the Torah Opens with Creation
topics.en: In the Holy Zohar (Bo 39b), Rabbi Yitzchak said: The Torah should not have begun except from “This month shall be unto you the beginning of months” (Exodus 12:2) — what is the reason? Because it is the renewal / beginning of the moon, etc.

topics.h: Renewal of the Moon and the Search for Hashem
topics.en: Behold, this is called “the renewal of the moon” (shiruta de-sihara), as my revered father, my master and teacher, of blessed memory, explained: that in this world Hashem established the principle, “If you seek Him, He will be found by you” (I Chronicles 28:9),,. meaning that to the extent that a person searches and inquires after His divine will, so does Hashem illuminate him, showing that He grants space and reality to man’s spiritual labor.,. And in truth, the essential seeking of man is that which he inquires and strives to establish holiness upon the physical body as well, and this is termed “the renewal of the moon” the moon representing the receptive vessel and physical existence.

topics.h: Why Darkness Appears at the Beginning
topics.en: However, this is the reason the Torah opened with “Bereishit” (Creation); for in truth it is written: “And darkness was upon the face of the deep,” ):: and my revered grandfather, my master and teacher, of blessed memory, raised a difficulty: For whom was there darkness at that time? Is it not written concerning Hashem (Psalms 139:12): “Even darkness obscures not from You, and the night shines like the day; darkness is as light”!

topics.h: Primordial Light Must Be Enclothed
topics.en: Rather, it is because Hashem willed that His divine light should clothe itself within the cognitive grasp and vessel of creation;,, and since the primordial light was still completely overt and transcendent before creation, and creation possesses no capacity to absorb such an explicit, unmasked light, this condition is perceived from the vantage point of creation as “darkness”;,:),. as it is stated in the Holy Zohar (Balak 204b): “The primordial light with which the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world — the world was unable to endure it. What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He fashioned light within light, and glory within glory, to enclothe one within the other.”

topics.h: Concealment Creates the Possibility of Choice
topics.en: And on account of this concealment and enclothing that Hashem established — that this light should be concealed in garments within garments — there branched out in this world the illusion wherein a person can imagine that he has the ability to act contrary to His divine will, heaven forbid.:),. Yet Hashem deliberately instituted this dynamic, as is stated in the Holy Zohar (Bo 34a): “One must know good and know evil, and turn oneself consciously toward the good.”:). And likewise it is stated in the Holy Zohar (Tetzaveh 184a): “There is no true light except that light which emerges out of darkness.”

topics.h: Breaking Through the Garments of Darkness
topics.en: That is to say: precisely because Hashem set before man such dense garments, to the extent that it can seem to him that he can act against His will, and yet man, through his divine service, pierces through every kind of concealing garment — this is the ultimate triumph, and this is what is termed “turning oneself consciously toward the good.”,,. And in truth, the essence of man’s piercing the concealment is that he implants and establishes sanctity over all the operational limbs of his bodily actions; herein lies the focal point of man’s divine service.

topics.h: Torah and Avodah Pierce the Separating Screens
topics.en: And this is the inner intent of the holy Ari, of blessed memory (Likutei Torah, Parashat Bereishit, s.v. Bereishit): “The Torah did not speak in the realm of Atzilut (Emanation), but only in Beriah (Creation).”,. Meaning, the essence of service exists solely because Hashem erected separating screens, and man, through Torah and spiritual labor, breaches the dividing screen and reaches the light of Hashem — that is the primary labor of humanity.

topics.h: Reaching the Hidden Utterance of Bereishit
topics.en: And in truth, if a person breaks through all manner of screens and reaches the first explicit utterance termed “Let there be light,” then Hashem grants him a portion even in the transcendent utterance of “Bereishit,”:). concerning which it is taught in the Talmud (Megillah 21b): “Bereishit is also an utterance.”, And even in this concealed utterance does Hashem grant a portion to man, for the service of Israel reaches even to this sublime origin,,",. and Hashem reveals to man that the entire reality of creation’s garmented descent in this world was instituted solely because He desired to bestow ultimate goodness upon His creatures, willing that it be called “the toil of man’s own hands” rather than unearned bread of shame; therefore He set up this concealment.: Yet in truth, the ultimate station of Israel is rooted even in the primordial utterance of Bereishit, designated as “Bereishit is also an utterance.” )

sections.title: Shabbat: The Purpose and Completion of Creation
sections.summary: The rest of Shabbat reveals that human effort and even the limits of creation ultimately originate with Hashem.

topics.h: Opening Text
topics.en: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. And the earth was unformed and void..”

topics.h: Shabbat as the Goal of the Six Days
topics.en: -':. “A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day: It is good to give thanks to Hashem” (Psalms 92:1-2). My revered grandfather, my master and teacher, of blessed memory, explained regarding this that the ultimate purpose of the creation of heaven and earth is the Sabbath day.

topics.h: Workday Effort and Shabbat Rest
topics.en: Meaning, during the six workdays, man acts and toils, and it appears to him that he himself is piercing the concealment and recognizing the revelation of the Kingdom of Heaven in the world., And afterwards, on the Sabbath day, man realizes: “What was the world lacking? Rest; the Sabbath came, rest came” (Rashi on Genesis 2:2) —

topics.h: The Divine Source of Human Strength
topics.en: meaning, he recognizes that even the very strength to toil was entirely granted by Hashem, and he recognizes that in truth, from the perspective of Hashem, all is without limit and without boundary;,. and that these boundaries which Hashem instituted were solely because He desired to bestow good upon His creations, wishing that the Jew should coronate Hashem through free choice, actively choosing the good and despising the bad.,. For had the revelation of the Kingdom of Heaven been completely explicit, there would be no free will whatsoever, as all would clearly recognize that it is impossible to flee from the Source of Life; therefore Hashem established these limitations.

topics.h: Boundless Expansion and the Command to Stop
topics.en: And from Hashem’s vantage point, it is as taught in the Talmud (Chagigah 12a): “At the time the Holy One, blessed be He, created His world, it expanded continuously like two balls of warp- threads,”,", meaning that from Hashem’s side existence expands boundlessly without limit or end; and when Hashem uttered “Let there be,” it kept expanding,", and only for the sake of the vessel of creation did Hashem say “Dai” (Enough!), thereby imposing these finite borders.

topics.h: Creation Is Limited for the Sake of Man
topics.en: And as my revered grandfather cited in the name of our master Rabbi Bunim of Przysucha, of blessed memory: This is the meaning of Hashem saying “Dai” — that there is enough (day) Heavenly glory brought forth through this measured creation.,",:). And as it is in the Holy Zohar (Emor 94b): It is not written “For in six days” (be-sheshet), but “For six” (ki sheshet) — meaning that this concealment itself is an intentional creation of Hashem.

topics.h: Shabbat Reveals a New Light
topics.en: And when man labors through all six workdays and breaks through the concealment, and on Shabbat recognizes this truth, Hashem then grants him renewed strength to serve Him in the subsequent six workdays with even greater elevation and greater vigor.

sections.title: Tohu and Bohu: Humility in the Face of Divine Revelation
sections.summary: Spiritual attainment demands increasing humility rather than a mistaken sense of independent greatness.

topics.h: Opening Text
topics.en: And the earth was unformed (tohu) and void (bohu).”

topics.h: The Inner Meaning of Tohu and Bohu
topics.en: It is stated (in Sefer HaBahir, §2): “Tohu is something that confounds/misleads human beings; Bohu means ‘it is in it’ (bo hu).”

topics.h: The Danger of Pride After Spiritual Success
topics.en: The meaning of this is: when Hashem shows a person that He validates and grants space to his divine service, the person must then serve Hashem with even greater humility and must not assume personal pride or assertiveness simply because Hashem revealed that his toil holds significance;,, rather, he must labor, fence himself in, and constrict his ego even further, recognizing that there is no independent perfection in creation, but that true perfection resides solely with Hashem;

topics.h: The Foolish and the Wise Before the King
topics.en: as it is written in the Holy Zohar (Beshalach 51b): “One who sees the King’s countenance radiant — he who is foolish says, ‘Behold, the King’s face is shining so all is lighthearted and free’; but he who is wise says, ‘The King is truly whole and righteous, yet judgment is sitting in concealment.’”,. That is, one who is foolish, when Hashem gives validation to his service, immediately assumes self-importance and boldness.,. However, one who is wise claims no personal power for himself, but hedges and disciplines himself all the more.

topics.h: Bohu: Finding the Divine Source Within
topics.en: And this is: “Tohu is something that confounds people” — meaning that creatures can be misled into drawing haughty self-assurance from it.,,",: And this is: “Bohu — it is in it” (bo hu), as my revered father explained: that in this very realization that Hashem desires his service, from that very thing Hashem expects the Jew to serve Him with even deeper devotion.

sections.title: Yom Echad: Divine Oneness Beyond Number
sections.summary: The first day alludes to a unity above created categories, which becomes manifest through the Mishkan and human service.

topics.h: Opening Text
topics.en: And there was evening and there was morning, one day.”

topics.h: Why the Torah Calls It One Day
topics.en: It is stated in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 3:9; Naso 13:8): If it follows the counting of days, it should have stated “a first day” (yom rishon), etc.

topics.h: Oneness Within and Beyond Number
topics.en: And this corresponds to what is taught in Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 22): “The Holy One, blessed be He, is called ‘One’ within number, and He is called ‘One’ beyond number.” ". “One beyond number” refers to that which is entirely above the grasp of creation; and “One within number” refers to His manifestation within the framework of creation.,":, And this is what the Midrash asks: “If it is according to the count of days,” meaning since creation has already begun here, it ought to have said “a first day” in series; A Dwelling for Hashem and a Place for Human Effort:. and the Midrash answers: Rather, from the time when the Holy One, blessed be He, was completely alone in His world, He yearned to possess a dwelling place among the lower realms., Meaning, Hashem reveals to you through this that following man’s divine service, Hashem shows him that He grants him a place even in that transcendent plane where Hashem is called “One beyond number” —,. namely, in that primordial realm where Israel arose in divine thought at the very beginning, even there is there a place for man’s labor.

topics.h: The Mishkan Reveals the Meeting of Heaven and Earth
topics.en: And this is what the Midrash concludes: “And when did He repay them? At the erection of the Mishkan (Tabernacle), as it is written (Numbers 7:12): ‘And he that presented his offering on the first day..’”, Meaning, there in the Mishkan they visibly witnessed how human mortal action unites with the infinite light of Hashem:,. namely, man saw that for the physical wealth he relinquished for his sacrifice, a heavenly lion of fire descended and consumed it; and all these physical vessels and the Mishkan were merely outer garments for the place of the Ark, which miraculously took up no physical space.,":,: And this is the meaning of: “When did He repay them? At the erection of the Mishkan” — for there everyone recognized how Hashem affords standing to the labor of man even above their limited grasp, from the realm where Hashem is called “One beyond number” as well.

sections.title: The Lower Waters: Concealment, Yearning, and Revelation
sections.summary: The separation of the waters becomes a model for seeking divine glory amid perceived distance.

topics.h: Opening Text
topics.en: And God said: Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear; and it was so.”

topics.h: Why the Second Day Lacked “It Was Good”
topics.en: It is stated in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 4:6): Why was “that it was good” not said on the second day? Because the work of the waters was not completed; therefore on the third day, when the work of the waters was finished, “that it was good” was doubled — once for the work of the waters and once for the work of the day.::)'. The explanation of this Midrash is according to what is taught in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 5:3): Rabbi Berechiah said: When the lower waters were separated from the upper waters, they separated only in weeping, etc.

topics.h: The Lower Waters Cry to Draw Near
topics.en: And my revered father explained regarding this that the weeping of the lower waters is like the parable in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 2:2): “And the earth was unformed and void” — a parable to two servants bought with one coin and on the same contract;,. for one the king decreed that he be sustained from the royal palace, and for the other he decreed, “If he does not toil, he shall not eat.” That second servant sat bewildered and despondent, etc.,. For in truth, from the perspective of Hashem, there is no difference between the upper waters and the lower waters, because at their root they are unified as one.

topics.h: The Waters and the Song of Praise
topics.en: And as my revered grandfather remarked: Why is it that in the psalm (Psalms 148) “Praise Hashem from the heavens,” the waters under the heaven are not mentioned — it explicitly mentions the upper waters, so why not the lower waters as well?.," And even though it says there “deeps” (tehomot), “deeps” does not refer to the water itself, but to the deep oceanic vessel that holds the water. Why then does it not list the lower waters themselves?,,',. The answer is: that chapter speaks of when beings stand to praise Hashem; and at the time of praising, there are no “lower waters” at all, for everything is elevated and considered “upper waters.”

topics.h: Upper and Lower as States of Divine Awareness
topics.en: For the concept of upper and lower waters is this: the upper waters stand in immense clarity before Hashem, whereas the lower waters represent concealment, where the mind of man becomes intensely perturbed and disoriented.:. And the source of this turmoil is because, as found in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer (ch. 10) and Midrash Tanchuma, Jonah ben Amittai said: “We do not find His overt glory in the sea.”

topics.h: The Sea and the Distress of Concealment
topics.en: And whenever a person does not see clearly the Heavenly glory rising from a situation, the mind of man becomes deeply distressed;,.,. for in a place where a person perceives the divine glory that can yet be revealed, he is not so perturbed. But at sea, where it appears that “His glory is not found,” human consciousness is thrown into agitation.:). Regarding this, the Talmud states (Tamid 32a): “All who go down to the sea have their minds unsettled until they ascend back to dry land.”

topics.h: Separation Exists Only From the Human Viewpoint
topics.en: Yet this distinction exists entirely from our side; but from Hashem’s side there is no concealment or division at all, and everything is considered upper waters,::," as we find in the Talmud (Chagigah 15a) regarding Ben Zoma, who said: “I was gazing between the upper waters and the lower waters, and there is between them only about three fingerbreadths”; whereupon the Sages remarked: “Ben Zoma is still outside” —,. meaning that he perceived a separation between upper waters and lower waters, whereas in absolute truth at their root there is no division whatsoever.,',,. And this explains their weeping when they were separated, according to the aforementioned parable of two servants: upon the upper waters He decreed that they be sustained effortlessly from the King's palace, while upon the lower waters He decreed that without toil they shall not eat.

topics.h: The Third Day Completes the Work of the Waters
topics.en: And this clarifies the Midrash that on the third day the work of the waters was completed: namely, from that which was said on the third day, “Let the waters gather.. and let the dry land appear, and it was so,”,, which indicates that space is made available for whoever desires to recognize His divine glory; this itself proves that at the root they are entirely one with the upper waters with no distinction at all.

topics.h: The Hidden Praise Rising From Creation
topics.en: For so we find in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 5:1): From the beginning of the creation of the world, praise to the Holy One, blessed be He, ascended from none other than the waters, etc. And what did they say? “Mightier than all in the heights is Hashem!” —. demonstrating that every cloud of concealment and perceived distance that exists concerning them stems entirely from our mortal perspective.,",",: And this is what is conveyed by “on the third day the work of the waters was finished”: from the fact that it says “and it was so” — that space is afforded for anyone who wishes to serve Hashem — this is the ultimate sign that they too stand in pure clarity before Hashem.

sections.title: Ezer Kenegdo: The Help Hidden in Opposition
sections.summary: Challenge and resistance become instruments of spiritual discovery and genuine assistance.

topics.h: Opening Text
topics.en: And the Lord God said: It is not good that man should be alone.”

topics.h: Why Man Was Created Without a Helper
topics.en: My revered father, of blessed memory, explained: How can such phrasing apply to Hashem, as if only now He realized that it is not good for man to be alone, whereas prior to creation He had not foreseen this?,. Rather, this very condition was itself a deliberate act of creation by Hashem: that man should feel he finds no helper — meaning that within his own human perception, no immediate aid should be apparent.

topics.h: Assistance Comes Through Resistance
topics.en: And as my revered grandfather explained: “I will make him a helper opposite/against him (ezer kenegdo)” — within creation, every true assistance emerges specifically from that which opposes it;,,. that is, Hashem placed before man all manner of obstacles, and man progressively expands Heavenly glory, dissolves all the obstacles, and redirects everything face-to-face to Hashem — and then man realizes that from these very obstacles came his greatest divine support.

topics.h: Reish Lakish and the Power of Questions
topics.en: Just as it is related in the Talmud (Bava Metzia 84a): Originally, when Rabbi Yochanan stated a teaching, Reish Lakish would raise twenty-four objections against him, and Rabbi Yochanan would provide twenty-four resolutions, and consequently the teaching became vastly clarified and broadened. This illustrates that Hashem determined that all genuine breakthroughs and assistance must emerge specifically through an opposing force;

topics.h: Turning Opposition Into Help
topics.en: and this is the Rabbinic maxim: “If he merits, it is a helper (ezer); if he does not merit, it is against him (kenegdo).” “Merits” means if he overcomes all these impediments and removes them, he perceives that he has received the ultimate help, and that is “ezer”; but if not, heaven forbid, it remains an opposing adversary (“kenegdo”).

sections.title: The Glory of Concealment and the Work of Discovery
sections.summary: The apparent boundaries of creation conceal its dependence on the limitless Creator, whom human inquiry seeks to reveal.

topics.h: Opening Text
topics.en: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter, but the glory of kings to search out a matter” (Proverbs 25:2).

topics.h: God Conceals; Kings Search
topics.en: And it is stated in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 9:1): From the beginning of the book until here: “It is the glory of God to conceal a matter”; from here onward: “It is the glory of kings to search out a matter.”::)',:,. And likewise it is stated in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 1:5): Anyone who comes and says, “This royal palace was built on a site of sewers, dung heaps, and foul garbage” — does he not slander and degrade it? So too, anyone who comes and says, “This world was created out of primordial chaos (tohu and va-bohu)” — does he not degrade it?! Astonishing!

topics.h: The Mystery of Limits in an Infinite Creation
topics.en: And the meaning is: a person might question — since all of creation descended from His divine Word, which is eternally living, enduring, boundless, and infinite, surely His manifested Word should likewise appear eternally living, enduring, and boundless;,. yet in this physical world it sometimes appears as though severed from His divine Word, and this suggests that the King of kings does not will His holy Name to be associated with degradation.

topics.h: Human Discovery as the Purpose of Concealment
topics.en: Indeed, it says “the glory of kings is to search out a matter” — meaning, since Hashem desired to bestow goodness upon His creatures and willed that finite creation should internalize His divine light, He deliberately structured creation to be bounded by limits and measure.,. However, from Hashem’s true vantage point there is neither limit nor measure, for in truth He is living, enduring, boundless, and infinite, and creation exists in utter perfection.

topics.h: The Heretic’s Challenge to Creation
topics.en: And this explains the dialogue where a certain heretic said to Rabban Gamliel: “Your God was a great artist, but He found pre-existing raw pigments with which He fashioned the world: tohu, bohu, and darkness”; to which he replied: “Regarding all of them explicit creation is written!” etc. (Bereishit Rabbah 1:9).,:,:,. The explanation is that the heretic’s philosophical claim was: Since Hashem is boundless and infinite, how could there possibly emanate from such a Will an entity defined by finitude and limits? Rather he argued, He must have encountered separate primordial materials: tohu and bohu.

topics.h: The Primal Forces Are Not Independent Powers
topics.en: For these primal forces are immense cosmic forces, as the Talmud states (Chagigah 12a): “Tohu is a green line that encompasses the entire world, etc.,” and regarding Bohu it is taught (Sefer HaBahir): “A thing that has substance”;, meaning, the heretic believed there existed an independent cosmic power outside of His divine will, asserting that from Hashem’s pure will alone it were impossible for bounded existence to emerge.

topics.h: Hashem Alone Creates Every Limit
topics.en: To this the Sage replied: “Regarding all of them explicit creation is written” — proving that in absolute reality there is no other force, and everything was created out of His simple, unified Will which is boundless and infinite., ),: Yet because His benevolent Will yearned to bestow good upon His creatures, He established in this world that every entity be bounded by measure and boundary (and these matters are profound; examine the introduction to the holy book Beit Yaakov Sha'ar HaEmunah, page 101, and you will understand).

sections.title: Noach and the Enduring World of Tikkun
sections.summary: Noach inaugurates a sustained world in which concealment itself gives creation a voice of longing and prayer.

topics.h: Opening Text
topics.en: And Noah begot three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.”

topics.h: Three Sons and Three Spiritual Conditions
topics.en: In the Holy Zohar (Noach 62a): A parable of a man, etc.: this one is righteous, this one is wicked, and this one is intermediate.

topics.h: From the Shattered Worlds to Olam HaTikkun
topics.en: My revered father, my master and teacher, of blessed memory, explained regarding this that the primary beginning of the World of Rectification (Olam HaTikkun) began from Noah onward. For prior to Noah, existence was still within the state of the “worlds that were destroyed” (almin de-itcharavu).,".. -':', And as we see, previously it is written (Genesis 4:1-2): “and she bore Cain.. and she bore further his brother Abel” — where there was as yet no cohesion or connection between one and the other;,":,. whereas from Noah onward the World of Rectification began, and here it is written: “Shem, Ham, and Japheth” linked together with the connecting 'vav' and direct accusatives, indicating that they possessed mutual connection and integration.

topics.h: Why the Earlier Worlds Were Destroyed
topics.en: And concerning the concept of the “worlds that were destroyed,” as taught in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 9:2): “This teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, created worlds and destroyed them, saying: ‘These do not please Me, but this one pleases Me.’”,:)': And in truth, how can such an idea apply to Hashem — that He should create worlds and subsequently need to destroy them? Is it not written concerning Him (Isaiah 46:10): “Declaring the end from the beginning”!

topics.h: How Creation Gains the Right to Pray
topics.en: Rather, the inner purpose of this is because Hashem willed that creation should possess a genuine plea, claim, and prayer before Him.,. Yet in truth, how could any creature possibly have a valid claim against Hashem? For a created being has no entitlement whatsoever before its Creator., Rather, the principal foundation of any claim creation can put forward is precisely where Hashem first reveals His light to man — meaning, when He grants him an experiential grasp of the divine Will —

topics.h: Loss of Light Gives Rise to a Cry
topics.en: and subsequently that light is concealed from him; then man has a justified cry and prayer: “Why have You lifted us up only to cast us down?”,, And likewise here: because Hashem desired that creation should possess a standing to cry out and beseech, He emanated worlds and revealed to them His will for their existence,:,. and then He concealed this from them, whereby creation was imbued with that heartfelt cry and prayer: “Why have You elevated us and then cast us down?”

topics.h: The Longing That Leads Toward Restoration
topics.en: And so it is stated in the Holy Zohar (Shelach 169a): In the future, the ultimate resurrection of the dead will be generated from the spiritual residue of the bones (hevlei de-garmei) and from the deep inner grief/yearning (itzavon) of man.:)':',. That is to say, for in truth it is written (Genesis 6:6): “And He was grieved at His heart.”:):, And in truth, how does “and He was grieved at His heart” apply to Hashem? Is it not written (I Samuel 15:29): “For He is not a man that He should repent or change His mind”!

topics.h: Yearning Remains Embedded in Creation
topics.en: Rather, all this is expressed from man’s side — meaning that within every single person there remained an indelible yearning pain and an ongoing cry.:). And so it is taught in the Holy Zohar (Bereishit 26a): “And a mist (ed - rose up from the earth” — this refers to the letters Aleph-Dalet ( - of the divine Name Adonai. And all of this reflects the yearning cry that creation possessed from the very initial awakening of divine Will, wherein Hashem willed the actualization of the worlds.

topics.h: Noach Establishes an Enduring World
topics.en: And the primary World of Rectification commenced from Noah, as it is written (Job 26:11): “The pillars of heaven tremble and are astonished at His rebuke.”,, And as my revered grandfather, of blessed memory, explained: this refers to the divine restraining rebuke (ge'arah) that remained impressed within each and every existence after the Flood — establishing that they should never again expand beyond their proper bounds —,: and this was the foundational establishment of the World of Rectification, endowing them with enduring existence for all eternity.
